claims.text: A homogeneous single-phase CrFeCoNiX microstructure promotes formation of a coherent protective oxide above 900 °C.
A homogeneous single-phase microstructure produces a slower-growing oxide scale than a multiphase microstructure.
A homogeneous single-phase microstructure produces a more adherent oxide scale than a multiphase microstructure.
A single-phase microstructure ensures a uniform distribution of alloying elements.
A single-phase microstructure minimizes local lattice and compositional mismatch at the oxide–substrate interface.
A multiphase microstructure creates local compositional variations that induce heterogeneous oxidation.
Local compositional variations cause non-uniform oxide growth.
Non-uniform oxide growth increases oxide-scale misfit stresses.
Higher oxide-scale misfit stresses increase the risk of cracking and spallation.
Single-phase alloys facilitate uniform oxide nucleation and oxide–substrate lattice matching.
Compositional gradients and grain-boundary effects in multiphase alloys disrupt oxide–substrate interfacial coherence.
Even distribution of Si, Mn, or Al supports controlled oxidation and formation of a continuous protective oxide.
Depending on the reactive element, the protective oxide may be epitaxial, uniformly nanocrystalline, or amorphous.
Minimal lattice mismatch and low interfacial defect density cause strong oxide adhesion.
Under identical 900–1100 °C exposures, the single-phase variant will show less cracking and spallation than the multiphase variant.
Similar oxide uniformity, coherence, and cracking or spallation resistance in both variants would falsify the proposed microstructural mechanism.
The proposed comparison holds nominal alloy composition and exposure conditions constant while changing the single-phase versus multiphase microstructure.
Environmental contaminants and exposure beyond 300 hours may alter oxide-scale behavior.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis makes oxide–substrate lattice matching and interfacial coherence central, but the mechanism also permits an amorphous protective oxide, for which crystallographic lattice matching or epitaxial coherence is not defined in the stated sense.
The principal claim is framed for temperatures above 900 °C, whereas the stated test and applicability ranges include exactly 900 °C.
